label: defixs-finance.vercel.app
title: Defix-Finance | One-Stop DeFi Solution
reasons: This SPA's own bundled copy (the page is an empty-root div plus one JS bundle) says 'Click here to rectify all strange wallet issues.', 'CLAIM AIRDROP', 'MISSING/IRREGULAR BALANCE ... resolve missing or irregular balance issues', and 'ASSET RECOVERY', which is a fake wallet-rectification UI aimed at visitors.

The bundle includes a wallet picker naming real products 'Trust Wallet', 'WalletConnect', 'Coinbase Wallet' together with 'Fixed WalletConnect issues', and contains a field named 'seedPhrase' — the sole purpose of such a UI is to get the visitor's wallet recovery phrase.

This is not a legitimate wallet-service page: no real wallet provider asks a visitor to fix 'strange wallet issues' or claim airdrops by entering their seedPhrase on a third-party host; that phrase is the credential used to drain a wallet.

label: igfree2026-lang.github.io/amazon-e-gift-card
title: Amazon Gift Card
reasons: Page claims "YOU WIN AMAZON GIFT CARD" and "Amazon $1000 USD Digital Gift Card (Email Delivery)" with no Amazon affiliation, no contest terms, and no winner-selection mechanism documented anywhere in the page source.

The only user action is the "Get Your Free Card Now" button, which links directly to effectivecpmnetwork.com, a third-party traffic/affiliate network unrelated to Amazon, indicating the visitor is funneled into a monetization scam.
The page uses the Amazon logo and an unauthorized gift-card prize premise to induce clicks, but discloses no operator and offers no mechanism to ever deliver a card.

label: rectifyesvalidation.vercel.app
title: EVM Resolve
reasons: The page funnels all visitors into a wallet-connect flow: the header button is 'CONNECT' and every CTA, including 'Assets Recovery', 'Wallet Validation', 'Claim Airdrop' and 'Restore your Account', redirects to '/connect/index.html'.

It uses the classic 'safe test transaction' pitch: 'The project rectification protocol (PRP) will define a test transaction to perform activities required on chain and does not have real effects on accounts connected' plus '100% Gas Refunds', pushing visitors to approve an on-chain action they are told is harmless.

The page seeds real wallet-pairing infrastructure — a hidden walletlink URL with a secret, a Web3Modal container, and a verify.walletconnect.com iframe — and then disables right-click/inspection ('Disable F12, Ctrl+Shift+I, Ctrl+U, and Ctrl+Shift+J'), consistent with a wallet-validation drainer front end.

label: login-app.vercel.app
title: Sign In
reasons: The page source includes a login form with fields "userid" and "pass", both required, posted to https://irreverent-request.000webhostapp.com/Login?App/insert1.php on an unrelated external host, not to any service authentication system.

The visible page is composed entirely of screenshots of a "Sign In" screen hosted on i.postimg.cc, with a password input and a submit image button overlaid on top, and no actual service, company name, signup flow, or account recovery logic.
The page is tagged noindex/nofollow and its only substantive behavior is asking the visitor for a username and password, demonstrating that the visitor's credentials are being exfiltrated off-site.

label: ertiga2154-ai.github.io/Cyber-Portofolio-
title: CYBER_PORTFOLIO // ARMAN SK
reasons: The page calls navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition and sends the visitor's precise GPS coordinates, IP (via ipapi.co), device model (via navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues) and battery level to https://api.telegram.org/bot${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/sendMessage with a hard-coded bot token and chat_id 7929149510 visible in the source.

The visible status box advertises the collection ('VISITOR_IP: FETCHING...', 'GPS_LIVE: REQUESTING PERMISSION...', 'BATTERY_LEVEL: SCANNING...') but never discloses that the data is transmitted to a private Telegram chat under the operator's control.

sendTelegramAlert() is called even when GPS permission is denied, transmitting the visitor's IP, OS and 'User Denied GPS Permission' to Telegram — there is no opt-in, disclosure, or way for the visitor to stop the exfiltration.

label: cpecctrummed.github.io/freemessages
title: Mail Settings - Loading...
reasons: The page is a login gate labeled 'Sign in using your receiving email and password' with fields 'Receiver Email Address' and 'Password' and a 'VIEW FILE' button under 'Secured Login Session', pretending to verify a visitor's email account to let them view a file.

Source hardcodes TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN '8413158165:AAH-5IUoUNZ1_Jyt5MA_OapUyGHIXkadLgA' and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID '8586537210', and sendToTelegram() POSTs the email, password, IP, country and browser to https://api.telegram.org/bot${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/sendMessage on every submit.

Each failed attempt displays 'Invalid password. Please enter the correct password.' and re-prompts up to 4 times to collect more credentials, while ipinfo.io is fetched to geolocate the victim; page also blocks right-click/F12/Ctrl+U to hide the harvesting code.

label: freekickmatch.github.io/obodo
title: Mail Settings - Loading...
reasons: Page titled 'Mail Settings - Loading...' asks for 'Receiver Email Address' and 'Password' with 'Sign in using your receiving email and password' copy and a 'VIEW FILE' button.

Form submission calls sendToTelegram which POSTs email, password, IP, country, and user agent to `https://api.telegram.org/bot8413158165:AAH-5IUoUNZ1_Jyt5MA_OapUyGHIXkadLgA/sendMessage` using hardcoded TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID '8586537210'.

The page impersonates the victim's mail provider by loading mail.google.com/mail.yahoo.com/outlook.live.com in an iframe and copying its favicon/title, then blocks right-click/devtools/source/print and forces up to 4 password retries before redirecting away.

label: secureai.vercel.app
title: Warden AI
reasons: The loaded app.js runs window.init(...) immediately on page load and silently reads connected wallet data from localStorage WalletConnect sessions, window.ethereum, and Solana/Solflare providers, then POSTs the wallet address to api.chainaware.ai API endpoints.
The same script computes a FingerprintJS visitor ID and sends it along with the wallet address in these background requests, without any visible disclosure on the page.
The script fetches banner-config from api.chainaware.ai and injects banners/modals based on the visitor's wallet risk profile and fingerprint data, with no consent or opt-out visible.

label: phantomtrace-ai.vercel.app
title: PHANTOMTRACE AI
reasons: PhantomTrace AI's bundled app code contains https://paypal.security-check.example-login.com/account/verify?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fpaypal.com, a PayPal-branded login/verification URL on a non-PayPal domain.
The page HTML is only an empty root div plus this script, so the phishing URL is the app's own content rather than a framework or third-party-library string.
The /account/verify path and redirect back to paypal.com create a credential-phishing flow aimed at the visitor's PayPal account.
